text:
Ana D: Quick heads-up - Saw CompetitorX push a "Lite" plan targeted at early-stage startups. Landing page calls out 50% cheaper token pricing and a lower-throughput SLA. Thought: this is showing up in our telemetry as a pricing signal from smaller trial accounts. Do we want to chase parity or lean into a differentiated thin-tier?
Mike R: Agree we should respond, but need numbers before changing roadmap. Can we quantify churn/upgrade impact if we don't ship a cheaper tier? cc @Jordan P
Jordan P: From product POV I'd prefer a differentiated thin-tier vs straight parity. Parity invites a price race. Options: (1) price-led lite (feature-subset + lower SLA), (2) capability-led lite (same price, limited features like no streaming or no reranking). Both need clear launch criteria.
Sam K: Engineering warning: building a separate pricing tier often spawns config branching. If we do (1) we should reuse existing runtime and enforce throttles via routing policy + quota limits, not separate binaries. Avoid long-lived forks.
Olivia C: Proposed launch criteria for Lite: 1) <5ms additional median latency from baseline for core gen paths, 2) unit-cost < 60% of standard for 1k token typical session on our infra, 3) GA docs + billing flow working, 4) guardrails for data residency matched to plan. If any of these fail, we don't GA.
Ana D: +1 on measurable criteria. Also want customer-facing story: "predictable low-cost for prototyping" vs "lite for cost-sensitive production". Messaging affects conversion.
Mike R: For next steps: can Eng run a 2-week spike to simulate lite pricing under existing infra (batching config + kv-cache adjustments)? Jordan, could PMs scope the exact feature subset for both options? Sam - can you estimate risk of rollback complexity?
Jordan P: I'll draft two candidate scopes by EOD Fri: price-led subset and capability-led subset. Will include acceptance tests and a short AB idea for conversion metrics.
Sam K: Spike estimate: 2 dev-weeks + 1 SRE week for rollout safeguards if we go price-led. If capability-led (feature gating), maybe 3 dev-weeks but simpler runtime work. Risk notes: quota enforcement + billing edge cases.
ProductBot: Dashboard update: telemetry filter "trial_accounts < $500/month" shows a 12% lift in signup-to-trial dropoff after CompetitorX announcement. Link: https://dash.redwood.example/telemetry/market-pricing-signal
Olivia C: Can Marketing prep two CTAs depending on direction? One focused on "Lite: prototype cheaply" and one on "Lite: production-grade cheap plan". Also need pricing threshold experiments (A/B price at -25% vs -50%).
Ana D: Ok plan: Jordan drafts scopes + acceptance tests by Fri. Eng runs spike (Sam owns), SRE on standby. Olivia and Mike will sketch pricing test matrix. We'll reconvene Monday for go/no-go. If anything changes ping here.
Mike R: Noted. I'll add a row to roadmap backlog and tag as "market-pricing-signal". Thanks.
Jordan P: Adding a quick experiment idea: route 10% new trials to a config that disables streaming + reduces batch size to test cost.
Sam K: If we do that, add a monitoring runbook to detect OOMs and slowdown regressions. I'll draft it.
Olivia C: Also need billing QA: prorations, upgrade/downgrade paths, and invoice previews for enterprise customers.
Ana D: Thanks team. Small ask: keep thread lean - just updates. We'll convert to a spec doc if we decide to proceed.
ProductBot: Reminder: Weekly roadmap sync scheduled Mon 09:30.
